title: Vineyard Sites
body: A vineyard site is more than an empty patch of land. Soil, climate and terrain influence its suitability, and a cultivar that suits one site may be less comfortable at another.

Use a Soil Probe on suitable land for a soil reading, or use the Almanac on vineyard land for a fuller survey. The Almanac can also report current seasonal conditions, weather and cultivation protection. General advice helps you choose what to investigate; the tool reading describes the place you are actually standing in.

Compare sites before establishing a large planting, then inspect the vines as conditions change. Preparing suitable soil and choosing appropriate cultivation measures are part of tending the site, not a guarantee of the same harvest every year.

Vineyard land and a registered estate plot are separate concepts. After founding an estate, sneak-use the Almanac at two opposite vineyard corners to register a plot. The survey bookmark and your plot records remain in Vintner's tools.
